what.text: This page follows refugees from Egypt living in the United States, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 10821 Egyptian refugees in the United States, 45.5% of all refugees from Egypt.
The United States is the largest host of Egyptian refugees, followed by France, Germany and the United Kingdom.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Egypt from 1993 to 1998, in 2014 and in 2017 to 2019, and with the Islamic State group from 2015 to 2022.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2013 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1990 at 5 refugees.
The figure reached its highest point, 14359, at the end of 2020, and was lower by the end of 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
These are year-end totals for the United States only, reported to UNHCR.
